clue.text: Attempt to enter into part with lines getting excessive zeal

indicators.note: one word is told to go inside another, so the attempt sits within the part

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece of something
to have a go is to make an attempt
RY, short for railway, is the crossword stand-in for lines

explanation.surface: Someone trying to get involved in a political party along with its policy lines turns fanatical.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerant, overzealous attachment to one's own opinions, so excessive zeal describes it loosely.

clue.text: Stagger round the bend on the way back

indicators.note: travelling back means the word for crazy is read from right to left

parts.note: round the bend is British slang for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: A driver lurches around a corner while returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish them, a verb synonym of stun.

clue.text: Performs tricky ascent

indicators.note: a tricky arrangement suggests the letters of ascent are jumbled

explanation.surface: A climber does a difficult climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a role or scene is to perform it, a simple verb synonym.

clue.text: State goodwill may bring disaster

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation of California, a US state
amity means friendly goodwill between people

explanation.surface: Political sermon suggesting a country's good relations may lead to catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a serious misfortune, a direct synonym of disaster.

clue.text: Overindulge one's head in pedantry

parts.note: to stuff yourself is to eat too much
one is the Roman numeral I
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: Advice that indulging one's mind leads to fussy precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffiness is a prim, narrow-minded formality, close kin to pedantic attention to rules.

clue.text: Spots infection

definitions.meaning: the disease is known for the red spots it brings out on the skin
it is a contagious viral illness

explanation.surface: A rash shows up that signals a contagious illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is a viral infection marked by a spotty red rash, matching both senses.

clue.text: Hearing and seeing red piano going

indicators.note: going means departing, so the musical letter leaves the word

parts.note: someone seeing red is furious, or spitting with rage
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A listener at a recital loses their temper as the pianist walks off.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hearing is a sitting, a session at which a case is heard.

clue.text: Restaurant's big cheese hotel disposed of

definitions.text: Restaurant's big cheese hotel disposed of

indicators.note: disposed of means thrown away, so that word is removed from the full title

parts.note: the head waiter in charge of a restaurant's dining room has a full French title ending in hotel
taken as written, the last word of that French title

explanation.surface: The head waiter has got rid of a hotel he managed.
explanation.walkthrough: The full French title is maître d'hôtel; dropping 'hôtel' leaves the familiar short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The head waiter running a restaurant's dining room is its boss, the big cheese.

clue.text: Amazed how the dentist likes me!

definitions.meaning: astonished, with jaw dropped in surprise
a dentist wants a patient's jaw wide apart to work on their teeth

explanation.surface: A patient jokes about the state the dentist prefers them in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone astonished gapes with jaw dropped, and the dentist wants a patient gaping literally.

clue.text: Our panic developed about company's wealth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the firm
developed suggests the letters of our panic are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Our alarm spreads through the firm's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges OUR PANIC to RNUOPIA, which goes 'about' CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia is a horn of plenty, an abundant supply, hence wealth.

clue.text: Swear experiencing initial temperature change is hassle

indicators.note: the first letter switches temperature scale, Celsius C becoming Fahrenheit F

parts.note: to cuss is to swear

explanation.surface: Someone curses as the thermostat changes, which is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss is bother or trouble, much like a hassle.

clue.text: A redneck's vacuous articles about South American

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters of redneck's remain
about means surrounding, so the two articles go round the compass letter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, and two of them are needed

explanation.surface: A hillbilly's empty talk is aimed at a man from the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' empties REDNECK'S to RS; AN and AN go 'about' S.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the state of Arkansas is an American.

clue.text: On stage in a cast giving needle

indicators.note: cast as in thrown around or moulded anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor in a theatre company gets annoyed while performing.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or irritate them, as does antagonise.

clue.text: No case for Lib Dems crushing Independent in the same place

indicators.note: the trimmed party squeezes the extra letter in its middle
the case of a word is its outside letters, so removing them leaves the middle

explanation.surface: The Liberal Democrats are left without a case after squashing an independent candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No case for' strips LIB DEMS to IBDEM, which is 'crushing' I. Lib Dems are the UK's Liberal Democrat party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin term used in footnotes to mean from the same source or place.

clue.text: Hackneyed standards for hi-fi buffs?

definitions.meaning: fixed, oversimplified images of a group, worn out by repetition
music enthusiasts might classify sound systems by type of stereo

explanation.surface: Clichéd tastes among audio enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a conventional, overused image; split as stereo types it suits hi-fi fans.

clue.text: Nonsensical banter about second staged protest

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the short moment
making no sense, so the letters of banter are scrambled

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: Silly chatter turns into a demonstration being organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonsensical' turns BANTER into RENTAB, which goes 'about' MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a crowd hired or organised to stage a demonstration.

clue.text: Lay out old money

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
the pound is British currency

explanation.surface: Laying out an old coin collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out or explain in detail, to lay out an argument.

clue.text: 'Time' certain to show deletion

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A clock certainly shows that something has been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is the act of rubbing out or removing, a deletion.

clue.text: Cross between love and longing welcoming good atmosphere

indicators.note: between places the cross in the gap separating the two pieces either side

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, like the letter O

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the longing holds the extra letter

parts.note: a yen is a longing
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A crossbreed of affection and desire makes for a pleasant mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is the vital gas in the air, a component of the earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Pretty as bananas hanging on a wall?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild

explanation.surface: A remark that something is as lovely as fruit dangling on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile hung on a wall as decoration.

clue.text: Antipathy under pressure is something Lance Armstrong became familiar with

definitions.text: something Lance Armstrong became familiar with

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming after the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
odium means hatred or strong dislike

explanation.surface: A cyclist under scrutiny faces hostility, as Lance Armstrong did.
explanation.walkthrough: Lance Armstrong, the cyclist, stood on many winners' podiums before doping disgraced him, hence the antipathy in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is the stand where race winners receive medals, familiar to a serial champion.

clue.text: Something old-fashioned in review of 'Brighton Rock'

indicators.note: review of says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the title's words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dated quality noticed in a critique of Graham Greene's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside BrightoN ROCk; 'review of' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn means trite, sentimental or dated material, so something old-fashioned fits.

clue.text: One who can tell a new code has been broken — it's about time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the time letter
a code that is broken is cracked open, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of cracking a new cipher at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been broken' turns A, N, CODE and IT'S into ANECDOIST, which goes 'about' T.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdotist is a teller of stories, someone who can tell a tale.

clue.text: Literally a mistake

parts.note: read as letter-ly, an error in the letters themselves, like a slip at the keyboard

explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing error, a mistake in the letters.

clue.text: Mark 'Waterloo Sunset' group losing head taking drug

indicators.note: losing its head means the band's first letter is dropped

parts.note: the Kinks, the British 1960s rock band who recorded Waterloo Sunset
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A rock band loses its leader to drugs and is stained by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kinks were a London rock band; Waterloo Sunset was their 1967 hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkspot is a blot or mark left by ink.

clue.text: Claim to express contentment about Post Office sorting centre

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the purr goes round the mail initials

parts.note: a cat purrs to show contentment

indicators.note: the centre is the middle letter of the word sorting

explanation.surface: A complaint about a mail-sorting centre, voiced with satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To purport is to claim or profess, a verb synonym.
